name: Acumatica
description: Acumatica is a cloud ERP platform for small and midmarket businesses, unifying financial management, distribution, manufacturing, project accounting, retail/POS, and CRM in one system. Instead of charging per user, Acumatica prices primarily by which applications a customer implements plus expected transaction volume and resource/data usage, with unlimited user access included under its published Customer Bill of Rights.
best_for: Small and midmarket companies — including construction, distribution, manufacturing, professional services, and retail businesses — that want unlimited user access to a single cloud ERP without paying per-seat licensing fees.
features: Financial management: multi-entity/intercompany accounting, payroll, and reporting tools
Distribution and inventory management: sales and purchase order management, warehouse management (WMS), and requisition management
Manufacturing management: bill of materials/routing, MRP, advanced planning and scheduling, and product configurator
Project accounting and resource management for professional services firms
Retail and point-of-sale (POS) with commerce connectors for Amazon, BigCommerce, and Shopify
Built-in CRM alongside the ERP modules
Reporting, dashboards, and AI-assisted automation aimed at repetitive tasks and anomaly detection
Unlimited user access included under Acumatica's licensing model rather than sold as per-seat licenses
pros: Pricing is based on the applications implemented and actual usage rather than per-user seats, per Acumatica's published Customer Bill of Rights
Unlimited user access is included rather than priced as a per-seat add-on
Serves multiple industry verticals (construction, distribution, manufacturing, retail, professional services) with dedicated modules
cons: No published dollar pricing — cost depends on which applications, deployment option, and expected transaction/resource volume, confirmed only through a partner or sales quote
Because pricing is consumption-based rather than a flat per-user list price, cost is harder to estimate upfront without an ROI/pricing calculator or sales conversation

tiers.name: Acumatica ERP
tiers.notes: Priced primarily by which applications/modules are implemented, plus expected transaction volumes and resource/data usage as users and transactions grow — not by per-user seat count. Unlimited user access is included. Acumatica publishes no specific dollar figures; pricing is confirmed via Acumatica or an authorized reseller, aided by industry-specific (Construction, Manufacturing, Distribution) online calculators.

alternatives.name: NetSuite
alternatives.description: Oracle's cloud ERP system unifying accounting, inventory, and order management with multi-subsidiary financial consolidation.
alternatives.best_for: Growing and mid-market companies wanting a single cloud system for financials, inventory, and order management, including multi-subsidiary consolidation.
strengths: Broad module coverage in one suite

alternatives.name: Sage Intacct
alternatives.description: A cloud financial management platform focused on core financials, multi-entity consolidation, and dimensional reporting for mid-market companies and nonprofits.
alternatives.best_for: Mid-market finance teams and nonprofits that need strong multi-entity consolidation and fund accounting without a full operational ERP.

alternatives.name: SAP Cloud ERP
alternatives.description: SAP's cloud ERP line led by SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, a subscription-priced ERP with embedded AI and industry-specific best-practice processes.
alternatives.best_for: Larger enterprises that want SAP's industry best-practice processes and are prepared for an SAP-led implementation.

alternatives.name: Odoo
alternatives.description: An open-source, modular business platform covering accounting, inventory, manufacturing, and more as individually priced apps.
alternatives.best_for: Smaller and mid-sized businesses that want to pay only for the ERP modules they actually use, with an open-source/self-hosting option.
